## The Itch — Neutral on Paper, Not in Fact

A model gets signed off as *neutral* because it passes the usual check:
near-zero correlation with the sensitive variable $S$.  But correlation only
sees straight lines.  An honest audit — a measure that catches *any* shape —
shows the score bending with $S$ all along.

This is the fairness mirror of the dependence chapter's [bad
morning](../dependence/01-correlation.qmd): **the number said safe, the
dependence was there.**

```{python}
#| label: fig-fair-hook
#| fig-cap: "Left: predictions look neutral — Pearson ≈ 0 against S. Right: binned, the score bends with S all along, and CKA reports strong dependence."
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 700
S = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
score = (S**2 - 1) + 0.4 * rng.normal(0, 1, n)  # nonlinear, ~zero correlation

pear = pearsonr(score, S)[0]
ck = cka_rbf(score, S)

fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2))

axL.scatter(S, score, s=12, c=COOL, alpha=0.5, edgecolors="none")
axL.set_title("The standard check", fontsize=12)
annotate_box(axL, 0.5, -0.10, f"Pearson(score, S) = {pear:+.2f}   ← looks neutral")
despine(axL)

bins = np.linspace(S.min(), S.max(), 11)
idx = np.digitize(S, bins)
centers = 0.5 * (bins[:-1] + bins[1:])
means = [score[idx == k].mean() for k in range(1, len(bins))]
axR.scatter(S, score, s=10, c=COOL, alpha=0.18, edgecolors="none")
axR.plot(centers, means, "-o", c=CRASH, lw=2.2, label="mean score per bin")
axR.set_title("The honest audit", fontsize=12)
annotate_box(axR, 0.5, -0.10, f"CKA(score, S) = {ck:.2f}   ← strongly dependent")
axR.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False)
despine(axR)

for ax in (axL, axR):
    ax.set_xlabel("sensitive variable S"); ax.set_ylabel("model score")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The Objective — The Whole Chapter in One Line

```
loss = fit(y_hat, y) + mu * Dep(y_hat, S)
```

`fit` is your usual prediction error.  $\operatorname{Dep}$ is any dependence
measure from [Chapter 1](../dependence/index.qmd), now applied between the
*predictions* and $S$.  The weight $\mu$ trades accuracy against neutrality.
The [ladder](03-fair-kernel-learning.qmd) is just a sequence of choices for
$\operatorname{Dep}$, from cheap-and-blind to flexible-and-expensive.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Background — The Penalty Is a Lagrangian

What we actually want is a *constrained* problem: minimize prediction error
subject to "no dependence on $S$,"

$$
\min_{\theta}\; \mathbb{E}\,[\,\ell(\hat y_\theta, y)\,]
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \operatorname{Dep}(\hat y_\theta, S) = 0.
$$

Forming the Lagrangian turns the constraint into the additive penalty we train
with,

$$
\mathcal{L}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}\,[\,\ell(\hat y_\theta, y)\,]
+ \mu\,\operatorname{Dep}(\hat y_\theta, S),
$$

where $\mu$ is the Lagrange multiplier.  Sweeping $\mu$ from $0$ to $\infty$
traces the **Pareto frontier** between accuracy and neutrality — exactly the
[trade-off curve](03-fair-kernel-learning.qmd) this chapter builds to.  There is
no single "fair model"; there is a curve, and $\mu$ chooses your operating point.
:::

## Two Framings, One Operation

The same objective wears two names in finance:

- **Fairness.** $S$ is a protected attribute (sex, race, age).  Regulation —
  the EU's [GDPR](https://gdpr.eu/) Art. 22 on automated decisions, and the
  **EU AI Act**, which classes credit scoring and CV screening as *high-risk* —
  requires that decisions not depend on such attributes.  A credit model must
  approve on ability to repay, not on group membership.
- **Factor-neutrality.** $S$ is a market or sector factor (beta).  A strategy
  that must be *market-neutral* should produce returns that don't load on the
  factor it is hedging.

"Don't discriminate" and "don't load on the factor I'm hedging" are the same
maths: drive $\operatorname{Dep}(\hat y, S)$ to zero.

::: {.eli5}
**One-liner.**  Fair learning doesn't *hide* the sensitive variable — it adds
"depend on $S$" to the bill, so the optimizer chooses to stop using it.
:::

Next: why the obvious fix — just delete $S$ — [doesn't
work](02-bias-and-proxies.qmd).
